lessons.title: The estimator lifecycle and a first baseline
lessons.motivation: Estimators and transformers have learned state and different output contracts.
lessons.progression: Trace constructor/fit/predict, then a separate transform-without-refit case.
lessons.terms: estimator, constructor, fit, predict, transform, fitted attribute, baseline.
lessons.math: A model maps features to predictions; a transformer maps features to features.
lessons.worked: DummyRegressor(strategy='mean').fit(X_train,[100,200,300]) predicts [200,200] for two test rows. Before fit it has no learned training mean.
lessons.misconception: Constructing an estimator is not fitting it; predict and transform are not interchangeable.

objectives.outcome: Respect the unfitted/fitted lifecycle and training/evaluation boundary.
objectives.assessment: Repair predict-before-fit or test-fit ordering and explain learned state.
objectives.remediation: Follow constructor→fit(train)→predict(new).

objectives.outcome: Predict a DummyRegressor training-mean baseline.
objectives.assessment: Select new baseline predictions and output length.
objectives.remediation: Compute the training target mean, not test mean.

objectives.outcome: Apply transform to new features without refitting.
objectives.assessment: Reject fit_transform on held-out data and justify transform.
objectives.remediation: Separate feature-state learning from prediction.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish browser fixture simulation from real notebook execution.
objectives.assessment: Choose what evidence establishes an actual fitted estimator.
objectives.remediation: Inspect the notebook execution manifest and fitted attributes.

lessons.title: Evaluate against a meaningful baseline
lessons.motivation: A metric answers a specific evaluation question relative to a fair baseline.
lessons.progression: Compute regression units, then inspect a majority-class baseline's missed positives.
lessons.terms: MAE, MSE, RMSE, accuracy, class balance, DummyClassifier, baseline.
lessons.math: Error units and denominators; majority-class accuracy can be misleading.
lessons.worked: Targets [100,200], predictions [120,180] give MAE=20, MSE=400 and RMSE=20 ($k). A 9:1 class split makes a majority predictor 90% accurate without recognizing positives.
lessons.misconception: Training score is not test performance; sklearn .score depends on estimator and is not always accuracy.

objectives.outcome: Compare a model against a training-fitted baseline on the same held-out rows.
objectives.assessment: Reject an unequal-split baseline comparison and explain the fairness boundary.
objectives.remediation: Align row IDs and training information for both predictions.

objectives.outcome: Choose and calculate an appropriate metric with units/denominator and reject majority accuracy as proof of positive-case detection.
objectives.assessment: Every form requires one regression metric/units decision plus an imbalance claim judged from the positive-case count table; the reason must justify the interpretation, not only name a metric.
objectives.remediation: Rebuild the per-row error/count tables in two staged examples before combining the decisions.

objectives.outcome: Interpret default score cautiously and name the explicit metric.
objectives.assessment: Choose R² versus classification accuracy meaning in a supplied API trace.
objectives.remediation: Read the estimator task and metric definition.

objectives.outcome: Separate improved validation metrics from causal/calibrated guarantees.
objectives.assessment: Select a limited conclusion from changed prediction vectors.
objectives.remediation: List which claims the data and metric actually measure.

lessons.title: Cross-validation keeps validation inside training
lessons.motivation: Cross-validation repeats train/validate boundaries inside the training set, not on the final test.
lessons.progression: Inspect one fold, then all folds, scorer sign and a group/time counterexample.
lessons.terms: fold, KFold, GroupKFold, TimeSeriesSplit, cross_val_score, negative scorer.
lessons.math: Repeated validation summaries; overlapping folds are not independent population experiments.
lessons.worked: For six training IDs, a declared three-fold split validates two IDs per fold; final-test IDs never appear. neg_mean_absolute_error values [-10,-20,-30] correspond to MAEs [10,20,30].
lessons.misconception: Cross-validation is not permission to use final-test rows; a negative sklearn loss scorer is not a negative physical error.

objectives.outcome: Keep validation/final-test rows out of fold fitting with the correct split unit.
objectives.assessment: Reject a leaking or group/time-inappropriate fold plan and explain the boundary.
objectives.remediation: Color-independent fit/validate/test ID tables.

objectives.outcome: Interpret negative loss scorers and aggregate declared fold scores.
objectives.assessment: Select mean MAE from signed scorer outputs.
objectives.remediation: Convert the sign before reporting units.

objectives.outcome: Recognize limitations of small-fold variability.
objectives.assessment: Reject a universal-confidence claim from a few fold scores.
objectives.remediation: Compare sample sizes, overlap and data assumptions.

objectives.outcome: Choose reproducible splitter settings without assuming shuffling always helps.
objectives.assessment: Match time/group/random scenarios to configured splitters.
objectives.remediation: Review the future-use question and entity/time order.

lessons.title: A complete train-fitted pipeline
lessons.motivation: A complete pipeline is composed familiar contracts, not a new block of magic code.
lessons.progression: Trace numeric/categorical branches separately before the complete fold-local model.
lessons.terms: make_pipeline/Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, SimpleImputer, OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler, LinearRegression.
lessons.math: Compose fitted coordinate transforms and the existing linear prediction model.
lessons.worked: Use the 12 training housing IDs for a named numeric/categorical preprocessing pipeline and LinearRegression; cross-validation fits the entire pipeline separately per fold; only the selected frozen workflow predicts the four final-test IDs.
lessons.misconception: A pipeline is not a causal model or a shield against future-derived features; cross-validation outside the pipeline can leak.

objectives.outcome: Place all learned preprocessing inside the cross-validated estimator.
objectives.assessment: Repair external fitting and explain fold-local state.

objectives.outcome: Predict the fit/predict output contract and compare trusted notebook results.

lessons.title: Compare models without choosing on the test set
lessons.motivation: Selection and final evaluation are different experiments and must remain separated.
lessons.progression: Apply a fixed validation rule, then refit and inspect a declared tie/limited claim.
lessons.terms: model comparison, selection, validation protocol, refit, final evaluation, uncertainty.
lessons.math: Selection bias; one held-out score does not establish universal superiority.
lessons.worked: Two declared candidates—DummyRegressor and the existing LinearRegression pipeline—are compared by training-only CV MAE. Select by the predefined rule, refit on the training set, then evaluate once on the untouched test IDs.
lessons.misconception: The best test score cannot also serve as an unbiased final check after repeated test-guided selection; a tiny synthetic win is not a deployment certificate.

objectives.outcome: Select candidates without using final-test feedback.

objectives.remediation: Draw the selection/refit/final-test timeline.

objectives.outcome: Apply a predefined comparable metric/split and tie policy.
objectives.assessment: Choose a winner or declared tie from changed CV score tables.
objectives.remediation: Compare identical folds and the stated tolerance/tie rule.

objectives.outcome: Refit the chosen workflow and communicate a reproducible limited result.
objectives.assessment: Select the complete final report and held-out membership.
objectives.remediation: Use the notebook manifest, chosen parameters and provenance.

objectives.outcome: Interpret introductory model-comparison uncertainty without ranking guarantees.

from sklearn.model_selection import KFold, GroupKFold, TimeSeriesSplit, cross_val_score

from sklearn.exceptions import NotFittedError
train = np.array([[1.],[2.],[3.]])
target = np.array([100.,200.,300.])
new = np.array([[4.],[5.]])
model = DummyRegressor(strategy='mean')
try:
    model.predict(new)
except NotFittedError:
    before = {'tag':'error','class':'NotFittedError'}
model.fit(train,target)
result = {'before_fit':before,'training_mean':model.constant_,'new_predictions':model.predict(new),'fit_ids':['H01','H02','H03'],'new_ids':['H04','H05'],'test_target_fit_allowed':False}
cases.reason: Construction stores configuration, not the learned target mean. Fit learns from training features/targets; predict uses saved state on new features without learning their targets. An unfitted prediction raises NotFittedError, and fitting on test targets invalidates unseen evaluation.
cases.misconception: Constructing the estimator learns the mean, so predicting before fit or fitting on test targets is valid.
